guidance: Rest well and stay hydrated. Warm fluids like tea or soup can soothe a sore throat. Standard supportive care resolves this within 7-10 days. Saline nasal drops help with congestion.
precautions: Wash hands frequently
Avoid close contact with others
Cover mouth when coughing or sneezing
Do not share utensils or towels

guidance: Monitor temperature regularly. Stay hydrated, rest, and keep room ventilated. Use a damp cloth on forehead. Consult a physician if fever goes above 103°F (39.4°C) or lasts more than 3 days.
precautions: Do not self-prescribe antibiotics
Avoid cold baths which can trigger shivering
Keep track of temperature readings
Seek care if rash or seizures appear

guidance: Rest completely. Drink plenty of water and warm teas. Watch for breathing issues or chest pain. Antiviral medications work best if taken within 48 hours of symptom onset.
precautions: Isolate to prevent spreading
Wash hands and sanitize frequently touched surfaces
Annual flu vaccination recommended
Wear mask if caring for others

guidance: Rest in a quiet dark room. Apply a cold or warm compress to head or neck. Drink water as dehydration is a common trigger. Over-the-counter pain relievers can help if not contraindicated.
precautions: Limit screen time
Maintain good posture
Take regular breaks from work
Avoid skipping meals

guidance: Rest in a dark, quiet room. Apply cold compress to head. Stay hydrated. Prescribed migraine medications (triptans) should be taken early in the attack for best effect.
precautions: Identify and avoid personal triggers (stress, certain foods, sleep changes)
Maintain a regular sleep schedule
Do not overuse pain medications as it can cause rebound headaches
Keep a migraine diary

guidance: Replace fluids and electrolytes with ORS (Oral Rehydration Solution). Eat bland foods like rice, bananas, and toast (BRAT diet). Avoid dairy, fatty, or spicy foods until recovered. Usually resolves in 1-3 days.
precautions: Prepare ORS at home: 1 liter boiled water + 6 tsp sugar + 0.5 tsp salt
Wash hands thoroughly especially before eating
Avoid sharing food or drinks
Seek care if diarrhea lasts more than 3 days or blood appears in stool

guidance: Increase dietary fiber intake with fruits, vegetables, and whole grains. Drink at least 8 glasses of water daily. Exercise regularly. Avoid excessive use of laxatives.
precautions: Do not ignore urge to use toilet
Avoid highly processed and low-fiber foods
Establish a regular toilet routine
Consult doctor if constipation is persistent or accompanied by blood

guidance: Eat smaller, more frequent meals. Avoid eating 2-3 hours before bedtime. Elevate head while sleeping. Avoid trigger foods. Antacids provide short-term relief. Persistent symptoms need medical evaluation.
precautions: Avoid spicy, oily, and acidic foods
Limit tea, coffee, and carbonated drinks
Do not lie down immediately after eating
Avoid alcohol and smoking

guidance: Drink plenty of water (2-3 liters/day) to flush bacteria. Consult a doctor for antibiotic prescription — do not self-medicate. Complete the full antibiotic course even if symptoms improve.
precautions: Urinate after sexual activity
Wipe front to back
Avoid holding urine for long periods
Wear cotton underwear
Avoid perfumed soaps near genital area

guidance: Clean eyes gently with clean wet cloth from inner to outer corner. Wash hands frequently. Avoid touching eyes. Bacterial conjunctivitis requires antibiotic eye drops prescribed by a doctor.
precautions: Do not share towels, pillowcases, or eye makeup
Wash hands before and after touching eyes
Avoid wearing contact lenses until healed
Discard old eye makeup

guidance: Identify and remove the trigger (soap, fabric, plant, food). Apply cool compress. Use calamine lotion or hydrocortisone cream (short term). Keep skin moisturized. See a doctor if rash spreads or becomes infected.
precautions: Avoid known skin irritants
Wear protective clothing if handling chemicals
Do not scratch rash as it worsens infection risk
Use mild fragrance-free soaps

symptoms: pain worsened by hot or cold
guidance: Rinse with warm salt water. Clove oil applied to the tooth can temporarily reduce pain. Avoid very hot or cold foods. See a dentist as soon as possible — toothaches rarely resolve without dental treatment.
precautions: Brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste
Floss daily
Avoid excessive sugar intake
Do not ignore dental pain as it can spread to jaw or neck

symptoms: dull or sharp lower back pain
guidance: Rest but avoid prolonged bed rest. Apply ice for first 48 hours then switch to heat. Gentle stretches and walking help recovery. Pain relievers (paracetamol) can reduce discomfort. See doctor if pain radiates below knee or comes with numbness.
precautions: Lift objects by bending knees not back
Maintain good posture while sitting and standing
Sleep on a firm mattress
Exercise core muscles regularly

guidance: Apply warm compress over the ear for pain relief. See a doctor for diagnosis — bacterial infections require antibiotics. Do not insert objects into ear. Most mild cases in adults resolve on their own in 2-3 days.
precautions: Dry ears after swimming or bathing
Do not use cotton swabs inside ear canal
Avoid exposure to cigarette smoke
Treat respiratory infections promptly to prevent spread to ear

symptoms: thick yellow or green nasal discharge
guidance: Steam inhalation helps clear sinuses. Saline nasal irrigation is very effective. Stay hydrated. Acute bacterial sinusitis (lasting more than 10 days or worsening) needs antibiotic treatment.
precautions: Avoid allergens and tobacco smoke
Use humidifier in dry air
Blow nose gently one nostril at a time
Stay hydrated to thin mucus

symptoms: symptoms appear within hours of eating
guidance: Stop eating and rest. Sip ORS or clear fluids in small amounts. Avoid solid food until vomiting stops. Seek emergency care if symptoms are severe, if there is blood in vomit/stool, or if the person cannot keep fluids down.
precautions: Cook meat and fish to safe internal temperatures
Refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours
Wash hands before cooking
Avoid raw or undercooked eggs, meat, and shellfish
Check expiry dates on packaged food

guidance: Maintain a regular sleep schedule. Avoid screens 1 hour before bed. Create a dark, quiet, cool sleep environment. Avoid caffeine after 2 PM. Relaxation techniques (deep breathing, meditation) help. See doctor if insomnia persists more than 3 weeks.
precautions: Avoid long daytime naps
Do not use bed for work or watching TV
Limit alcohol as it disrupts sleep quality
Avoid heavy meals close to bedtime

guidance: Identify and avoid allergens (dust, pollen, pet dander). Antihistamines (cetirizine, loratadine) provide effective relief. Nasal corticosteroid sprays work well for persistent symptoms. Keep windows closed during high pollen seasons.
precautions: Use allergen-proof mattress and pillow covers
Vacuum frequently with HEPA filter
Shower after outdoor activities to remove pollen
Monitor air quality index in your area

symptoms: symptoms worsen with exercise or cold air
guidance: Always carry a prescribed rescue inhaler (Salbutamol). Use controller medications as prescribed even when feeling well. Avoid known triggers. During an attack: use rescue inhaler, sit upright, stay calm. Call emergency if no improvement after inhaler use.
precautions: Avoid smoke, dust, pollen, mold, and pet dander
Stay indoors during high pollution days
Cover nose in cold weather
Get annual flu vaccine
Never stop controller medication without consulting doctor

symptoms: rash progresses from trunk to face and limbs
guidance: Isolate to prevent spread. Calamine lotion and cool baths relieve itching. Cut fingernails short to reduce scratching. Avoid aspirin. Paracetamol for fever. Usually resolves in 5-10 days. Vaccination is the best prevention.
precautions: Do not scratch blisters to avoid scarring and secondary infection
Wash hands frequently
Isolate from pregnant women, newborns, and immunocompromised people
Keep child home from school until all blisters have crusted

symptoms: widespread red rash starting on face
guidance: Rest and maintain hydration. Vitamin A supplementation is important especially in children. Monitor for serious complications (pneumonia, encephalitis). There is no specific antiviral treatment; care is supportive. Vaccination (MMR) is the most effective prevention.
precautions: Isolate patient to prevent spread — measles is highly contagious
Ensure all household contacts are vaccinated
Keep room well-lit but avoid harsh light if patient is light-sensitive
Seek immediate care if breathing difficulties or seizures occur
